after: For each fixed mapping and edge, the numerator is the square of the mean, across ensemble members, of the square roots of their individual shot-variance coefficients. Each individual coefficient is the squared norm product minus the squared bias-subtracted prediction. The denominator is the population variance of the member predictions, with the ensemble size as divisor. The numerator divided by total shots per edge is the ensemble variance under continuous oracle-optimal allocation of independent unbiased shots. The denominator divided by the number of independent uniform exact-member draws is the member-sampling variance; this is distinct from the finite-population correction for distinct-member subsets above. The reported ratio divides these two coefficients, without equating the costs of a shot and an exact member evaluation. It does not use the separate synthetic unequal-cost allocation check. These coefficients compare different operations and sampling laws, and establish neither runtime, tail-risk nor planner dominance.
